Simplify the following powers of \(i\).

  • \(i^{34}=\)
  • \(i^{39}=\)
  • \(i^{44}=\)
  • \(i^{57}=\)

For any positive integer \(n\), we can evaluate \(i^n\) by determining the remainder when \(n\) is divided by 4.

Remainder of \(n/4\) \(i^n\)
0 \(1\)
1 \(i\)
2 \(-1\)
3 \(-i\)

In computer programming, the modulo operator returns the remainder. This operation is used so frequently, that it is often abbreviated to a single symbol (for example, in Python, 5%2 represents the remainder when 5 is divided by 2.)

I will represent the remainders using the Desmos notation.

  • \(\mathrm{mod}(34,4)=2\) so \(i^{34}=-1\)
  • \(\mathrm{mod}(39,4)=3\) so \(i^{39}=-i\)
  • \(\mathrm{mod}(44,4)=0\) so \(i^{44}=1\)
  • \(\mathrm{mod}(57,4)=1\) so \(i^{57}=i\)

To find the remainder using a scientific calculator, I would divide by 4, floor the result, multiply by 4, and subtract that amount from the original.

\[\mathrm{mod}(x,4)~=~x-4\cdot \left\lfloor\frac{x}{4}\right\rfloor\]

\[\sqrt{-150}\]

\[\sqrt{25}\cdot \sqrt{-1}\cdot \sqrt{6}\]

\[5i \sqrt{6}\]

The quadratic formula says if \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) then \(x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\).

The solutions to \(x^{2}+{16}x-{116}=0\) can be expressed, in simplest form, as \(x=h\pm p\sqrt{q}\), where \(p\) might be imaginary. Find the values of \(h\), \(p\), and \(q\).

\(h=\)

\(p=\)

\(q=\)

Write the equation.

\[x^{2}+{16}x-{116}=0\]

Identify the coefficients.

\[a=1\] \[b=16\] \[c=-116\]

Plug numbers into the quadratic formula.

\[x = \frac{-(16)\pm\sqrt{(16)^2-4(1)(-116)}}{2(1)} \]

Simplify.

\[x = \frac{-16 \pm \sqrt{256-(-464)}}{2}\]

Simplify.

\[x = \frac{-16 \pm \sqrt{720}}{2}\]

Use prime factorization.

\[x = \frac{-16 \pm \sqrt{2\cdot2\cdot2\cdot2\cdot3\cdot3\cdot5}}{2}\]

Isolate the twin factors.

\[x = \frac{-16 \pm \sqrt{2\cdot2\cdot2\cdot2\cdot3\cdot3}\cdot \sqrt{5}}{2}\]

Simplify the square root of the square.

\[x = \frac{-16 \pm 2\cdot2\cdot3\cdot \sqrt{5}}{2}\]

Simplify the integer products.

\[x = \frac{-16 \pm 12\cdot \sqrt{5}}{2}\]

Split the fraction.

\[x = \frac{-16}{2} \pm \frac{12\cdot \sqrt{5}}{2}\]

Both numerators contain a factor of 2.

\[x = -8 \pm 6\sqrt{5}\]

So, \(h=-8\) and \(p=6\) and \(q=5\).

The quadratic formula says if \(ax^2+bx+c=0\) then \(x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\).

Find the sum of the two complex numbers. \[(-4+7i)+(-9+8i)\]

For addition, just add the real components \((-4)+(-9)=-13\) and the imaginary components \((7)i+(8)i=15i\). \[-13+15i\]

Find the sum of the two complex numbers. \[(-5+3i)+(8-9i)\]

For addition, just add the real components \((-5)+(8)=3\) and the imaginary components \((3)i+(-9)i=-6i\). \[3-6i\]

Find the sum of the two complex numbers. \[(7+5i)+(-8+4i)\]

For addition, just add the real components \((7)+(-8)=-1\) and the imaginary components \((5)i+(4)i=9i\). \[-1+9i\]

Find the sum of the two complex numbers. \[(-9+2i)+(4-7i)\]

For addition, just add the real components \((-9)+(4)=-5\) and the imaginary components \((2)i+(-7)i=-5i\). \[-5-5i\]

Find the sum of the two complex numbers. \[(2-5i)+(-8-4i)\]

For addition, just add the real components \((2)+(-8)=-6\) and the imaginary components \((-5)i+(-4)i=-9i\). \[-6-9i\]

For addition, just add the real components \((7)+(8)=15\) and the imaginary components \((9)i+(-5)i=4i\). \[15+4i\]

For addition, just add the real components \((9)+(-4)=5\) and the imaginary components \((-5)i+(7)i=2i\). \[5+2i\]

For addition, just add the real components \((-7)+(5)=-2\) and the imaginary components \((-3)i+(-6)i=-9i\). \[-2-9i\]

For addition, just add the real components \((8)+(7)=15\) and the imaginary components \((1)i+(-2)i=-1i\). \[15-i\]

For addition, just add the real components \((1)+(9)=10\) and the imaginary components \((3)i+(-8)i=-5i\). \[10-5i\]
